questions.stem: Explain why proving P = NP or P ≠ NP would have significant implications for fields such as cryptography.
markingGuide: P = NP implies efficient solutions for all verifiable problems.
Cryptographic systems rely on certain problems being hard to solve.
If P = NP, many cryptographic systems could be broken.
P ≠ NP would confirm the security assumptions of cryptography.
questions.explanation: Proving P = NP would imply that problems assumed to be hard (like factoring) could be solved efficiently, threatening cryptographic security. P ≠ NP would support current security assumptions.
